title: Italian Geography and Climate
quiz.0.question: Roughly what percentage of Italy's land is hilly?
quiz.0.explanation: About 42% of Italy is hilly — the terrain best suited to growing vines.
quiz.1.question: What is the main climate type of northern Italy?
quiz.1.explanation: Northern Italy (e.g. Piemonte) has a mainly continental climate, with cold winters, hot summers and wide day-night temperature swings.
quiz.2.question: In which Italian regions are volcanic soils most common?
quiz.2.explanation: The areas around Etna in Sicily and Vesuvius in Campania have abundant volcanic soils.
quiz.3.question: Which of these is NOT a typical trait of southern Italian wines?
quiz.3.explanation: Southern Italy's hot climate usually gives rich, high-alcohol, fruity wines with relatively lower acidity.

slides.2.title: 🌡️ Three Climate Zones
slides.2.content:
🏔️ North — Continental Climate

Regions: Piemonte, Lombardy, Veneto

Traits: cold winters, hot summers, wide day-night swings

Style: high acidity, elegance, strong ageing potential

Key wines: Barolo, Amarone

🌿 Centre — Mediterranean Climate

Regions: Toscana, Umbria, Marche

Traits: warm, dry summers and mild winters

Style: balanced structure, complex flavours

Key wines: Chianti, Brunello

☀️ South — Hot Climate

Regions: Puglia, Sicily, Calabria

Traits: hot, dry and sunny

Style: rich, high alcohol, fruity

Key wines: Primitivo, Nero d'Avola
slides.3.title: ⛰️ The Influence of Terrain
slides.3.content:
🏔️

The Alps

Hillside and terraced vineyards, some above 1,000 m

Cool climate → high acidity, elegant style

Examples: Nebbiolo, Pinot Nero

🌄

The Apennine Hills

Tuscany's classic areas

Good drainage → concentrated flavours

Examples: Sangiovese, Trebbiano

🏝️

Volcanic Soils

Sicily's Etna, Campania's Vesuvius

Rich in minerals → distinctive flavours

Examples: Nerello, Aglianico

🌊

Maritime Influence

The coastal areas of Liguria and Sardegna

Sea breezes moderate → fresh style

Examples: Vermentino, Pigato
slides.4.title: 🍇 A Diversity of Soils
slides.4.content:
🪨 Limestone (Calcareous)
Piemonte (Barolo), Toscana
Good drainage, giving elegance and minerality
🧱 Clay
Toscana (Chianti), Umbria
Good water retention, full and powerful grapes
🌋 Volcanic
Sicily (Etna), Campania
Rich in minerals, distinctive flavours
⛰️ Marl and Sandstone (Ponca)
Friuli (Collio, Colli Orientali)
Good drainage, giving whites aroma and minerality
slides.5.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
slides.5.questions.0.question: Which main mountain range runs the length of the Italian peninsula?
slides.5.questions.0.explanation: The Apennines run from north to south through the whole Italian peninsula, shaping the climate and drainage of the whole country like a spine — Italy's most important geographical feature.
slides.5.questions.1.question: Which natural factors shape regional differences in Italian wine styles? (Select all that apply)
slides.5.questions.1.options.2: C. The brand fame of wineries
slides.5.questions.1.explanation: Latitude sets the base temperature; temperature falls about 0.6°C for every 100 m of elevation; soil affects minerality and acidity. Brand fame is a market factor and does not affect natural terroir.
slides.5.questions.2.question: What is the main contribution of Etna's volcanic soils to the local wines?
slides.5.questions.2.options.2: C. Distinctive minerality and volcanic-rock flavours
slides.5.questions.2.explanation: Etna's volcanic soils are rich in minerals, giving wines from grapes such as Nerello Mascalese a distinctive minerality and volcanic flavour — the core feature that sets them apart.
slides.5.questions.3.question: What is the most typical feature of northern Italy's continental climate?
slides.5.questions.3.options.0: A. Hot and dry all year
slides.5.questions.3.options.1: B. Distinct seasons, hot summers and cold winters, with typical autumn fog (nebbia)
slides.5.questions.3.options.2: C. Very little rain, close to a desert climate
slides.5.questions.3.explanation: The northern continental climate has distinct seasons with hot summers and cold winters. Autumn fog (nebbia) is typical of Piemonte, and the name Nebbiolo comes from it; it helps slow ripening and flavour complexity.
slides.5.questions.4.question: Which of these are important quality soil types in Italy? (Select all that apply)
slides.5.questions.4.explanation: Italy's soils are varied: limestone (Barolo, Chianti) gives drainage and minerality; volcanic soils (Etna) give distinctive mineral flavours; clay (Chianti, Umbria) retains water for full grapes. Italy has no permafrost.

slides.7.title: 🎓 Summary
slides.7.content:
✓ Spanning about 10 degrees of latitude, Italy has huge climatic differences
✓ Hilly terrain is the most suitable for growing wine grapes
✓ Elevation, exposure and soil together shape terroir
✓ The north is elegant, the centre balanced, the south rich
